A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOMCAT research and contain readable main text, Appendices A-I, and the checklist. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and prose.

before.justification: v1 reports original TOMCAT evaluations on four datasets in Tables 1-2, component ablations, and additional empirical comparisons and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, and appendix experiments. Retention of the earlier results still constitutes reporting original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same CLIP base model, knowledge accumulation modules, adaptive weights, priority-queue procedure, losses, and inference updates. The queue remains initialized as empty; the new limitation does not specify a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UT-Zappos, MIT-States, C-GQA, and Clothing16K with the same closed-world and open-world coverage. No additional dataset, task, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2, 9-10, and 17-18 retain identical comparator sets. The revised related-work description of TDA does not change its participation: Table 9 already distinguishes TDA [19] from online-TPS [53] in v1.

E3.justification: The splits in Table 7, hyperparameters in Table 8, evaluation metrics, feasibility calibration, and appendix comparison procedures are unchanged. No revised experimental setting accompanies the new queue-initialization caveat.

E4.justification: The component, loss, KAM-initialization, test-order, and hyperparameter ablations remain unchanged, as do the accuracy trajectories, runtime analysis, and case studies. No new analysis tests the newly stated priority-queue limitation.

E5.justification: Table 6 retains the same three test orders generated using different random seeds. Section 4.3 retains the same statement that their differences are not statistically significant, without changes to uncertainty reporting or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: The main-text and appendix results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains TOMCAT's UT-Zappos AUC values of 48.3 in the closed-world setting and 43.7 in the open-world setting; no numerical results, plotted trends, or case-study outcomes are added or removed.

T1.justification: The task definitions and Equations 1-17 are unchanged, including the adapter formulation in Appendix A and the cluster assumption and entropy-gradient reasoning in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and main conclusion retain the same TOMCAT contributions, claimed first use of unsupervised test-time data for CZSL, and performance claims across four benchmarks.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the limitation about backpropagation increasing test-time overhead with a warning that improper priority-queue initialization can bias predictions toward compositions already stored. The limitation about neglecting primitive-level knowledge remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, hardware, hyperparameters, runtime measurements, and license information remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same future code-release statement; v2 supplies no new initialization instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 changes TDA from a prototype-shifting method cited as [53] to a training-free adapter using a key-value cache and progressive pseudo-label refinement, cited as [19]. This corrects a limited prior-work characterization and attribution; the bibliography and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 moves the CZSL paragraph before the VLM paragraph. Other edits comprise the TDA and limitation sentences, capitalization of an Appendix E subheading, and the arXiv version/date stamp; the overall document structure is preserved.

P2.justification: Figures 1-10 and Tables 1-18 retain their displays, captions, structure, and placement. The prose edits introduce no distinct figure, table, or page-layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the TDA/TPS conflation in Section 2, bringing it into agreement with the bibliography and Table 9. The new queue-bias caveat identifies a specific failure condition, although it replaces the explicit latency warning without additional experimental support. Appendix G and Table 16 still disclose the overhead. The gain is therefore limited to reporting accuracy and qualification; the method and empirical evidence are unchanged.
